question: Some large cohorts find people who eat the least salt die sooner. What do critics chiefly suspect?
options: Low-salt diets run short of iodine
Sick people eat less, salt included
Low salt harms the heart directly
answer: Sick people eat less, salt included. Frail, ill and dieting people eat less of everything, so a low salt reading can mark illness rather than cause it. Many cohorts also judged intake from one urine sample, which swings day to day. The low end of the curve fills with the unwell.
move: When the sick do less of something, doing less of it looks deadly.
ask: When something looks risky among sick people, did the illness come first?
trap: Harm to the heart directly, the reading the curve seems to show.
source: Cobb et al., Circulation, AHA advisory, 2014
reference: Cobb et al., Methodological issues in cohort studies that relate sodium intake to cardiovascular disease outcomes: a science advisory from the American Heart Association, Circulation, 2014
